title: Altair Aether
note: Our own design: a ~300 kg lunar communications relay, fired off a mass driver near the lunar south pole into an elliptical frozen lunar orbit, built from real flight hardware where it exists. Frame: x along the track (the direction of travel, and the craft's axis: the launch load runs down it), z up, y left. The craft's separation plane is at x = 0; the sled and the rails are behind and below it. Pass 1: structure, tank, main thruster, sled and rails.

sep_ring_diameter.quote: Table 5-1, MLB15: A (outer stay-out diameter) 17.02 [in]; bolt circle 15.000 in, 24 fasteners

tank_diameter.quote: 80583-1 6,348 104.0 182.9 lb m hydrazine 83 kg hydrazine 23.13 ID (ICD for 80583) 589 ID 18.3 8.3 400 27.6 Parker Solar Probe
tank_diameter.note: the table gives only its inside diameter; a sphere of 104 L is 0.583 m across, so it is modelled as a 0.589 m sphere

orbit_periselene_alt.quote: Periselene altitude (km) 673 ("these parameters are indicative and may be subject to change")

constellation.quote: With only two properly phased relays in this type of orbit, South Pole coverage could be continuous
constellation.note: three: two for coverage and one spare

also.quote: Small spacecraft – as low as 150-300 kg could be adequate for the service

insertion_dv.source: design, computed: the speed at aposelene of the 673 x 7331 km orbit (vis-viva, moon_gm, moon_radius), all of it given there by the main burn after a near-vertical shot

dv_budget.source: design, chosen: insertion_dv plus phasing, station keeping and disposal

main_isp.note: the low end, for a blowdown tank

propellant_mass.source: design, computed: 300 kg x (1 - exp(-550 / (222 x 9.80665))) (rocket equation, standard gravity)

sep_ring_axial.quote: Maxium Line XLB (Axial) [lbf/bolt] 1,504 ("Values listed are 80% of qualification loads")
sep_ring_axial.note: 24 bolts; 300 kg at 14 g is about 41 kN, well inside

sep_ring_lower_height.source: design, estimate: the manual's table gives no total height

sep_ring_upper_height.source: design, estimate: the manual's table gives no total height

cone_length.source: design, chosen: separation ring up to the lower deck

sled.value: a pusher bulkhead bolted to the separation ring's lower half (the launch load), a base the craft's flat underside rests on (its weight in lunar gravity), four rail shoes and the linear motor's armature plate
sled.source: design, chosen: nothing like it flies yet

track_accel_g.source: design, computed: 1.68 km/s (circular speed at the surface, from moon_gm and moon_radius) over a 10 km track, v^2 / 2L

open_questions: Launch geometry: a shot from near the south pole puts the orbit's high point over the launch site only if the shot is near-vertical (about 2.1 km/s), not the 1.68 km/s horizontal shot the 14 g was worked out for. A horizontal shot from the south puts the high point over the north. Options: a track on a steep slope, a launch site further north, or a bigger burn to turn the orbit. The craft's structure is the same either way; the tank size here covers the vertical case.
Lunar Pathfinder's orbit differs between SSTL's guide (673 x 7331 km, 54.9°) and a 2022 NASA slide (500 x 7500 km, 57.8°); SSTL calls its values indicative.
A south-pole launch site reaches inclinations near 90° directly; the 54.9° orbit needs a site at or below about 55°S, or a plane change.
